title: The generic Kummer residue sheaf
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $C$ be a smooth connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves], and let $n\geq1$ be an integer invertible in $k$. Then $C$ is irreducible; let $\eta$ be its generic point [def-sc-generic-point], $K=k(C)$ its function field [def-sc-function-field], $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}K\to C$ also the canonical morphism, and $C_{\rm cl}$ the set of closed points of $C$ [def-weil-closed-points]. For $x\in C_{\rm cl}$ let $i_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to C$ be the closed immersion of the point and $v_x:K^\times\to\mathbf Z$ the normalized valuation of the discrete valuation ring $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ [def-sc-divisor]. On the small etale site of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ let $\mathbf G_m$ be the sheaf $V\mapsto\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)^\times$ [def-sc-gm-torsor] and $\mu_n\subseteq\mathbf G_m$ the subsheaf $V\mapsto\{u\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V):u^n=1\}$, so that $1\to\mu_n\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{u\mapsto u^n}\mathbf G_m\to1$ is the Kummer sequence on $\operatorname{Spec}K$; let $\delta:\eta_*\mathbf G_m\to R^1\eta_*\mu_n$ be its connecting morphism in the long exact sequence of the higher direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] of $\eta_*$. Let $\operatorname{div}:\eta_*\mathbf G_m\to\bigoplus_{x\in C_{\rm cl}}i_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z}$ be the divisor map of [lem-sc-divisor-sequence-general] for $X=C$ (whose codimension-one points are the closed points; on global sections it is $f\mapsto(v_x(f))_x$), and let $\underline{\mathbf Z}\to\underline{\mathbf Z/n}$ be the reduction map of constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then there is a unique isomorphism of etale sheaves on $C$

$$
\varphi:R^1\eta_*\mu_n\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\bigoplus_{x\in C_{\rm cl}}i_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z/n}
$$

with $\varphi\circ\delta=(\bmod n)\circ\operatorname{div}$. In particular the composite $K^\times=\Gamma(C,\eta_*\mathbf G_m)\xrightarrow{\delta}\Gamma(C,R^1\eta_*\mu_n)\xrightarrow{\varphi}\Gamma\bigl(C,\bigoplus_xi_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z/n}\bigr)$ sends $f$ to the section whose component in $\Gamma(C,i_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z/n})=\mathbf Z/n$ is $v_x(f)\bmod n$, for every $x\in C_{\rm cl}$; only finitely many of these components are nonzero.

proof.text:
*The divisor sequence on $C$.* By [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings], $C$ is a Noetherian integral scheme, every point other than $\eta$ is closed, and for every closed point $x$ the local ring $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ and normalized valuation $v_x$; by [lem-sc-smooth-regular] all local rings of $C$ are regular. So $C$ is an integral regular Noetherian scheme. Its codimension-one points are exactly the closed points: the codimension of $x$ is $\dim\mathcal O_{C,x}$, which is $1$ for a closed point (a discrete valuation ring) and $0$ for $\eta$ (a field). For a closed point $x$ with uniformizer $t$ and $f=ut^m\in\mathcal O_{C,x}\setminus\{0\}$, $u$ a unit, $\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{C,x}/f)=m=v_x(f)$, so the order $\operatorname{ord}_x$ of [lem-sc-divisor-sequence-general] is $v_x$; and $i_x$ is a closed immersion since $x$ is closed. Hence [lem-sc-divisor-sequence-general] gives the exact sequence of etale sheaves on $C$

$$
0\to\mathbf G_{m,C}\to\eta_*\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{\operatorname{div}}\bigoplus_{x\in C_{\rm cl}}i_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z}\to0,
$$

the first map being the unit $\mathbf G_{m,C}\to\eta_*\eta^*\mathbf G_{m,C}=\eta_*\mathbf G_m$.

source.place: Theorem Tag 03RI (etale-cohomology-theorem-fundamental-exact-sequence), for the smooth curve $X=C$

proof.text:
*$R^1\eta_*\mu_n$ is the cokernel of $n$ on $\eta_*\mathbf G_m$.* As $n$ is invertible in $k\subseteq K$, the Kummer sequence $1\to\mu_n\to\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{n}\mathbf G_m\to1$ on $(\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\Et}$ is exact by [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] (written additively, the middle map is multiplication by $n$). The functor $\eta_*$ is additive and left exact and $R^q\eta_*F=\mathcal H^q(\eta_*I^\bullet)$ for an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], i.e. $R^q\eta_*$ are the right derived functors of $\eta_*$ computed by injective resolutions; $\Ab((\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\Et})$ has enough injectives. So [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] gives the exact sequence

$$
\eta_*\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{n}\eta_*\mathbf G_m\xrightarrow{\delta}R^1\eta_*\mu_n\to R^1\eta_*\mathbf G_m.
$$

The last term is $0$ by [lem-sc-generic-r1-gm-vanishing]. Hence $\delta$ is an epimorphism with kernel the image of $n$, and induces an isomorphism $\bar\delta:\operatorname{Coker}(n:\eta_*\mathbf G_m\to\eta_*\mathbf G_m)\xrightarrow{\sim}R^1\eta_*\mu_n$ with $\bar\delta\circ\pi=\delta$, $\pi$ the cokernel map.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03PL (etale-cohomology-lemma-kummer-sequence) and Lemma Tag 03RJ (etale-cohomology-lemma-higher-direct-jstar-Gm), $q=1$; the long exact sequence is Derived Categories Lemma Tag 015B (derived-lemma-higher-derived-functors)

proof.text:
*Snake lemma.* Multiplication by $n$ (the $n$-th power map on units) is an endomorphism of each term of the sequence of step 1 commuting with its maps, since these are homomorphisms of sheaves of abelian groups. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-abelian] in $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ to the diagram with both rows that sequence and vertical maps $n$: the top row $\mathbf G_{m,C}\to\eta_*\mathbf G_m\to\bigoplus_xi_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z}\to0$ is exact with $\operatorname{div}$ an epimorphism, the bottom row $0\to\mathbf G_{m,C}\to\eta_*\mathbf G_m\to\bigoplus_xi_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z}$ is exact with the first map a monomorphism. Its six-term sequence ends with

$$
\operatorname{Coker}(n|_{\mathbf G_{m,C}})\to\operatorname{Coker}(n|_{\eta_*\mathbf G_m})\xrightarrow{\overline{\operatorname{div}}}\operatorname{Coker}\bigl(n|_{\bigoplus_xi_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z}}\bigr)\to0.
$$

The first term is $0$: $n$ is invertible in $k$ and $C$ is a curve over $k$, so the Kummer sequence of [def-sc-kummer-sequence] on $C$ is exact [lem-sc-kummer-exact], i.e. $n:\mathbf G_{m,C}\to\mathbf G_{m,C}$ is an epimorphism. Hence $\overline{\operatorname{div}}$, the map induced by $\operatorname{div}$ on cokernels, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Theorem Tag 03RI with Lemma Tag 03PL; the snake lemma is Homology Lemma Tag 010H (homology-lemma-snake)

proof.text: *The cokernel of $n$ on the residue sheaf.* In $\Ab(C_{\Et})$, which has all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], cokernels and direct sums are colimits and colimits commute with colimits, so $\operatorname{Coker}(n|_{\bigoplus_xi_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z}})=\bigoplus_x\operatorname{Coker}(n|_{i_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z}})$. Each $i_x$ is a closed immersion, hence finite, so $i_{x*}$ is exact [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] and $\operatorname{Coker}(n|_{i_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z}})=i_{x*}\operatorname{Coker}(n:\underline{\mathbf Z}\to\underline{\mathbf Z})$. On $(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x))_{\Et}$ the constant sheaf functor is sheafification of the constant presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], which is exact, and $\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{n}\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Z/n\to0$ is exact; so $\operatorname{Coker}(n:\underline{\mathbf Z}\to\underline{\mathbf Z})=\underline{\mathbf Z/n}$ with cokernel map the reduction. Together: the reduction maps induce an isomorphism $\rho:\operatorname{Coker}(n|_{\bigoplus_xi_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z}})\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_xi_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z/n}$ whose composite with the cokernel map is $\bmod n$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 03RL (etale-cohomology-lemma-cohomology-istar-Z): $i_x$ finite, Proposition Tag 03QP (finite higher direct image zero)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* Put $\varphi=\rho\circ\overline{\operatorname{div}}\circ\bar\delta^{-1}$, an isomorphism by steps 2–4. Then $\varphi\circ\delta=\rho\circ\overline{\operatorname{div}}\circ\pi=\rho\circ(\text{cokernel map})\circ\operatorname{div}=(\bmod n)\circ\operatorname{div}$. Since $\delta$ is an epimorphism (step 2), $\varphi$ is the only morphism with this property. Global sections: $\Gamma(C,\eta_*\mathbf G_m)=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}K,\mathcal O)^\times=K^\times$ by the definition of $\eta_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; on global sections $\operatorname{div}$ sends $f$ to $(v_x(f))_x$ (step 1), whose support is finite, and its component in $\Gamma(C,i_{x*}\underline{\mathbf Z/n})=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x),\underline{\mathbf Z/n})=\mathbf Z/n$ ($\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ is one point, $\kappa(x)=k$) is $v_x(f)\bmod n$.

split_report.summary: Statement made self-contained: the curve, generic point, closed points, valuations, mu_n on Spec K, the connecting map delta and the divisor map (of lem-sc-divisor-sequence-general) are introduced, and the isomorphism is characterized by phi∘delta = (mod n)∘div, with the global-sections formula f ↦ (v_x(f) mod n)_x that the citer lem-sc-second-kummer-divisors uses. The blueprint's hypotheses 'integral separated' are implied by 'smooth connected curve' of def-sc-curves (integral by lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings) and were dropped from the wording. The proof was rewritten following Stacks section 03RH: the fundamental exact sequence 0→G_m→η_*G_m→⊕i_{x*}Z→0 (03RI; the Lean-closed node lem-sc-divisor-sequence-general), the long exact sequence of η_* on the Kummer sequence of Spec K with R^1η_*G_m=0 (03RJ, q=1; new node lem-sc-generic-r1-gm-vanishing), the snake lemma with n surjective on G_{m,C} (lem-sc-kummer-exact), and the exactness of i_{x*} for the finite i_x. This replaces the blueprint's stalkwise argument (strict henselization stalk formula, Hensel's lemma for n-th roots, geometric stalks exact), which never constructed the comparison map as a sheaf map beyond 'after sheafification'. Dropped uses: prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula, prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact, lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr, cor-sc-hilbert-90-field (Hilbert 90 now sits inside the new node's proof).
